def factor_crash_vol_volume_simple(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    high = df_copy["high"]
    low = df_copy["low"]
    close = df_copy["close"]
    volume = df_copy["volume"]
    prev_close = close.shift(1)
    tr = np.maximum(high - low, np.maximum(np.abs(high - prev_close), np.abs(low - prev_close)))
    atr5 = tr.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
    atr20 = tr.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    ret5 = close / close.shift(5) - 1.0
    vol_ratio = atr5 / atr20.replace(0, np.nan)
    crash_signal = -ret5 * vol_ratio
    vol_ma20 = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    volume_ratio = volume / vol_ma20.replace(0, np.nan)
    factor = crash_signal * volume_ratio
    df_copy["factor_crash_vol_volume_simple"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_crash_vol_volume_simple"]
description: Simplifies the qualified parent 'factor_crash_corr_scaled' by removing the volume-price correlation divergence multiplier. The core crash mechanism (negative return amplified by expanding volatility) remains intact, weighted by volume above/below average to capture conviction. This ablation reduces over-parameterization and targets improved RankICIR by removing a potentially noisy interaction term. The cross-sectional z-score transform is preserved to highlight relative crash risk on each date.
